concerns.text: FR-010 mandates reporting the 'correlation between human coherence ratings and automated validity scores'. Tasks T020 (Cohen's κ) and T022 (rubric application) cover inter-rater reliability and rating collection, but no task exists to compute or report the statistical correlation (e.g., Pearson/Spearman) between the human scores and the automated metrics (T013-T015).

FR-001 requires generating '≥80 samples per prompt per strategy' using 'two open-source LLM checkpoints'. Task T008 targets only TinyLlama (1.1B) for CI. Task T011 targets 7B models but is marked 'local only' and excluded from CI. No task covers the generation of the full 80-sample dataset for the second checkpoint in the primary pipeline, leaving the 'two checkpoints' requirement unimplemented for the main study volume.

SC-001 requires metrics to be computed for '≥95% of generated reports'. Task T013 (NLI consistency) handles length errors by 'skipping pairs' but lacks a task to track the report-level completion rate or enforce the 95% threshold, risking silent failure to meet the success criterion.

Task T012 implements a 'control corpus' of technical reports. This scope is not present in the spec's User Stories or Functional Requirements (which define four prompting strategies for phenomenological reports). This is an unapproved addition not traceable to a spec ID.

Task T028 implements 'internal state tracing' (activations/attention maps). Neither the spec nor the plan defines capturing internal model states as a requirement for the defined validity metrics (NLI, embeddings, markers). This is an unapproved scope addition.

Tasks T045-T049 implement 'Advanced Review' features (Turing test, latent traces, embodiment gap) based on simulated reviewer comments. These capabilities are not reflected in the spec's User Stories or Functional Requirements, creating a disconnect between authorized scope and planned implementation.
